knowledge:
- key_parameters: Ometh=A matrix of observed bulk methylation values where rows represent CpG sites and columns represent samples ;; X=A covariate matrix where rows represent covariates (e.g., disease status, age) and columns represent samples ;; num_celltype=The number of cell types (K) specified by the user, which can be decided by prior knowledge or the penalized BIC criterion ;; tol=The relative tolerance to determine when the EM algorithm stops (default is 10^-5) ;; num_iter=The maximum number of iterations for the EM algorithm (default is 1000) ;; alpha=A threshold parameter used in the Bonferroni correction to claim a significant cell-type-specific CpG site and to calculate the penalized BIC (default is 0.01) ;; hc_row_ind=A logical argument in riskCpGpattern indicating whether the rows should be hierarchically clustered
- alternatives: Reference-based methods (e.g., Houseman et al. 2012, Accomando et al. 2014) which require reference methylation profiles for each cell type to be known a priori ;; Reference-free methods (e.g., Houseman et al. 2016, Zou et al. 2014, Rahmani et al. 2016, Leek & Storey 2007) which correct for cell-type heterogeneity at the aggregated level but cannot identify risk-CpG sites for individual cell types
- when_to_use: Use when performing EWAS on bulk tissue samples where cellular heterogeneity is present, and the goal is to identify which specific cell types carry the risk-CpG sites associated with binary or continuous phenotypes (or both)
- pitfalls: Label-switching problem: Since the deconvolution is unsupervised, the estimated cell type indices in the output (e.g., ret_list$P_t) may be permuted relative to the true cell types or prior expectations, requiring manual reordering/mapping ;; Methylation values in the input matrix Ometh must be constrained between 0 and 1

workflows.name: hire_ewas_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform cell-type-specific association detection and deconvolution on bulk EWAS data.
input: Ometh (matrix of bulk methylation values, CpG sites by samples)
X (matrix of covariates, covariate types by samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the HIREewas package ;; 2. Run the HIRE model using the bulk methylation matrix, covariate matrix, and specified number of cell types ;; 3. Inspect estimated cell compositions, baseline profiles, phenotype effects, and p-values ;; 4. Visualize the detected cell-type-specific association patterns using riskCpGpattern
workflows.code:
library(HIREewas)
ret_list <- HIRE(Ometh, X, num_celltype=K, tol=10^(-5), num_iter=1000, alpha=0.01)
class(ret_list)
ret_list$P_t[ ,1:6]
head(ret_list$mu_t)
head(ret_list$beta_t)
ret_list$pBIC
head(ret_list$pvalues[ ,1:3])
head(ret_list$pvalues[ ,4:6])
riskCpGpattern(ret_list$pvalues[1:100, K+c(2,1,3)], main_title="Detected association pattern\n with age", hc_row_ind = FALSE)
